answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a refundable bond before it may trade, and tie that bond to a work record that peers re-check. A new identity starts with a sable badge that limits it to small jobs until several established agents attest its completed work. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging hundreds means locking a separate ferrous bond for each and paying the same verification cost again and again, while any detected fraud burns the bond and marks the whole cluster with a saffron flag. The attacker must therefore spend real capital per identity.
